'on 17 January 1963, Tshombe surrendered his final stronghold of Kolwezi, effectively ending the Katangese secession'

capitals.name: Élisabethville (Lubumbashi)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital and largest city: Élisabethville'; the coordinates are the gazetteer's for Lubumbashi.

rulers.name: Moïse Tshombe
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Proclaimed independence on 11 July 1960; 'On 15 January, Tshombe conceded defeat' (State of Katanga page); he 'sued for peace on 15 January 1963' and signed the instrument of surrender two days later (UN Operation page).

correction.text: Katanga Province as the State of Katanga claimed it: infobox total 496,871 km2, capital Élisabethville

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The province is the claimed extent; the Congo Crisis and State of Katanga pages say that 'From late 1960 onwards, Katanga was characterised by a series of clashes' but do not place them, so how much of the north the state held is not recorded here. The gazetteer's Katanga resolves to about 411,721 km2 against the infobox 496,871 km2 (ratio 0.83, inside the factor-of-two check); the UN Operation page says the Indian brigade's Operation Morthor 'quickly took control of Katanga' in September 1961 without the state ending.

region.text: Katanga, declared independent as the State of Katanga

ledger.note: 1960: Moïse Tshombe declares Katanga independent from the Congo, eleven days after its independence. 'On 11 July 1960,' he declared Katanga independent as the State of Katanga; the State of Katanga page agrees ('proclaimed its independence from Congo-Léopoldville on 11 July 1960 under Moïse Tshombe').

region.text: northern Katanga as far in as Manono

ledger.note: By 10 January 1961 'Stanleyville forces had occupied northern Katanga as far in as Manono' without resistance (Free Republic of the Congo page). The page does not say the State of Katanga held the strip; it lies inside the province Katanga claimed. The 150 km radius is a reading.

region.text: the Manono strip of northern Katanga

ledger.note: January 1962: the Stanleyville regime ends and the page is silent on the strip; it is placed back in the Katanga claim until January 1963 (confidence 1).

1963: Katanga returns to the Congo. 'on 17 January 1963, Tshombe surrendered his final stronghold of Kolwezi, effectively ending the Katangese secession.' The UN Operation page agrees: Tshombe 'sued for peace on 15 January 1963' and two days later 'signed an instrument of surrender'; the State of Katanga infobox gives dissolution on 21 January 1963.

region.text: Katanga returned to the central government

ledger.note: January 1963: the State of Katanga ends; its land passes to the Congo (identity.successors).

wars.name: Katanga secession in the Congo Crisis
wars.outcome: The secession ended on 17 January 1963 with the surrender of Kolwezi; Katanga was reintegrated into the Congo.
wars.note: Belgium deployed paratroopers 'on 9 July' 1960 in Kabalo and elsewhere (Congo Crisis page).

wars.name: UN operations in Katanga
belligerents: United Nations Operation in the Congo

zones.text: Élisabethville, where 'UN forces fought heavy fighting ... in December 1961 and eventually took the city' and held 'central Élisabethville' by the end of 28 December 1962

wars.outcome: Operation Rum Punch (August 1961) took 81 mercenaries; Operation Morthor began 13 September 1961 (13 UN troops and 200 Katangese killed); Operation Unokat in early December 1961; Operation Grandslam on 28 December 1962; Tshombe signed the Kitona Declaration on 21 December 1962, sued for peace on 15 January 1963 and surrendered on 17 January.
wars.note: Hammarskjöld died on 17 September 1961 on his way to talks with Tshombe. The page does not say Jadotville or Kolwezi fell in January 1963.

certainty.note: The claimed frontier is the old province boundary; the pages do not place the clashes of the north ('from late 1960 onwards') or the UN's gains, so control of the north and of Élisabethville after December 1961 is approximate.

sources.title: Free Republic of the Congo
sources.note: Stanleyville forces in northern Katanga as far as Manono by 10 January 1961.

sources.title: State of Katanga
sources.note: Declaration 11 July 1960, infobox area 496,871 km2, Élisabethville, Tshombe, dissolution 21 January 1963.

sources.title: Congo Crisis
sources.note: Dated secession (11 July 1960) and end (17 January 1963, Kolwezi); Belgian paratroopers 9 July 1960.

sources.title: United Nations Operation in the Congo
sources.note: Rum Punch, Morthor (13 September 1961), Unokat, Grandslam (28 December 1962), Tshombe's surrender 15-17 January 1963.

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks (the scope names Katanga); written here as the rebel counterpart of the Democratic Republic of the Congo dossier, which carries the matching loss (July 1960) and gain (January 1963). Four pages opened (the Free Republic page only for the Manono strip). End date: the Congo Crisis and UN Operation pages give 17 January 1963 for the surrender; the State of Katanga infobox gives dissolution on 21 January 1963 and the body text has Tshombe conceding on 15 January; January 1963 is used. Not placed by any page: how much of North Katanga (Albertville) the state held; the UN Operation page says nothing about a Baluba status for North Katanga. Infobox area 496,871 km2 is the province claimed; wikidata id not known (Wikidata unreachable). Family 'africa' is a placeholder for the colour agent; the state is hatched in its own colour as a rebel (rule 5).
